questions.question: Who was the Prime Minster of India when the Fundamental Duties were first incorporated in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indira Gandhi**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indira Gandhi** was the Prime Minister of India when the Fundamental Duties were first incorporated in the Constitution of India.
 
• The Fundamental Duties were added by the **42nd Amendment Act** of the Constitution in **1976**.
 
• The amendment added a new part, Part IV-A, which consists of a single Article, **Article 51A**, that enumerates the Fundamental Duties of citizens.
 
• The idea of Fundamental Duties was inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.
 
• These duties are intended to serve as a constant reminder to citizens that while enjoying their rights, they also have certain duties towards the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **42nd Amendment Act** is also known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to the large number of changes it brought to the Constitution.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by law.
 
• There are currently **11 Fundamental Duties** listed under Article 51A, which include duties such as respecting the national symbols, cherishing the noble ideals of the freedom struggle, and protecting the sovereignty and integrity of India.
 
• These duties are meant to promote a sense of discipline and commitment among citizens towards the nation.

questions.question:
Who said the following?

“Money is what money does.”
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prof. Walker**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Prof. Walker** is credited with the statement "Money is what money does."
 
• The statement emphasizes the functional definition of money, focusing on its role and activities in the economy rather than its intrinsic properties.
 
• Money serves several key functions: a medium of exchange, a unit of account, a store of value, and sometimes, a standard of deferred payment.
 
• This perspective aligns with the pragmatic approach in economics, where the utility and effectiveness of money are determined by its practical applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prof. Walker** was an influential economist whose work significantly impacted monetary theory.
 
• The pragmatic view of money has been pivotal in understanding its evolving forms, from physical currency to digital money.
 
• This definition underscores the adaptability of money to different economic contexts and technological advancements.
 
• Understanding the functions of money helps in grasping the broader economic principles and the impact of monetary policy.

questions.question: Rohini Bhate, Pandit Munnalal Shukla, Kumudini Lakhia and Uma Sharma are famous exponents of which of the following classical dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rohini Bhate, Pandit Munnalal Shukla, Kumudini Lakhia, and Uma Sharma** are renowned exponents of the classical dance form **Kathak**.
 
• **Kathak** is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance.
 
• This dance form traces its origins to the **traveling bards of ancient northern India known as Kathakars or storytellers**.
 
• Kathak dancers tell various stories through their hand movements, footwork, facial expressions, and eye work.
 
• The dance form is characterized by intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures and is traditionally performed to the accompaniment of classical Hindustani music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak** has three main gharanas (schools) which are the **Lucknow, Jaipur,** and **Benares** gharanas, named after the cities where the Kathak dance tradition evolved.
 
• The Lucknow Gharana emphasizes graceful movements and facial expressions, while the Jaipur Gharana focuses more on the footwork and spins.
 
• The Benares Gharana combines elements of both and is known for its unique style and presentation.
 
• Today, Kathak is performed not only in India but also globally, with many artists and institutions dedicated to its preservation and promotion.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Indian political party system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Single party system**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India has a **multi-party system**, which means that multiple political parties can and do contest elections across the country.
 
• A **single party system** is a system in which only one political party is legally allowed to hold power, which is not the case in India.
 
• The presence of numerous political parties in India leads to the formation of coalition governments, especially at the central level.
 
• The **lack of effective opposition** and **factions and defections** are also features seen within the Indian political party system due to the diverse and fragmented nature of the electorate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indian political party system is characterized by a high level of **political pluralism**.
 
• There are several national and regional parties that play significant roles in the political landscape of the country.
 
• The Election Commission of India oversees the electoral process to ensure free and fair elections across the country.
 
• The Indian Constitution provides for a democratic system of governance, ensuring the representation of diverse groups and interests.
 
• Coalition politics is a common phenomenon in India due to the multi-party system, especially in forming governments at both the central and state levels.

questions.question: The fundamental vocabulary of __________ dance constitutes mock combat techniques, stylised gaits of birds and animals and movements modelled on the chores of village housewives and mostly performed by male dancers in Eastern India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhau**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chhau** dance is a traditional Indian dance form that originates from Eastern India, particularly from the states of West Bengal, Jharkhand, and Odisha.
 
• The dance incorporates elements of martial arts, mock combat techniques, and movements inspired by animals and birds, making it unique and visually striking.
 
• Chhau dance is traditionally performed by male dancers who often wear elaborate masks and costumes.
 
• The themes of Chhau dance performances are usually derived from Indian epics like the Ramayana and Mahabharata, as well as local folklore and nature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chhau** dance has three styles named after the locations where they developed: Purulia Chhau (West Bengal), Seraikella Chhau (Jharkhand), and Mayurbhanj Chhau (Odisha).
 
• Unlike the Purulia and Seraikella styles, Mayurbhanj Chhau is performed without masks.
 
• UNESCO inscribed Chhau dance in the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.
 
• The dance form combines elements of both classical and folk traditions, making it a rich cultural heritage of India.

questions.question: The Red Fort is located in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Delhi**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Red Fort** is situated in **Delhi**, the capital city of India.
 
• It was constructed by the Mughal Emperor **Shah Jahan** in the mid-17th century.
 
• The fort served as the main residence of the Mughal emperors for nearly 200 years, until 1857.
 
• It is an iconic symbol of India's rich history and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The Red Fort is named for its massive enclosing walls of red sandstone and is a prominent tourist attraction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Delhi** is a city rich in history and has many other significant landmarks such as the Qutub Minar, India Gate, and Humayun's Tomb.
 
• Every year on **Independence Day** (15th August), the Prime Minister of India hoists the national flag at the main gate of the Red Fort and delivers a nationally broadcast speech from its ramparts.
 
• The architecture of the Red Fort reflects a blend of Persian, Timurid, and Indian styles.
 
• Major structures within the fort include the Diwan-i-Aam (Hall of Public Audience), Diwan-i-Khas (Hall of Private Audience), and the Rang Mahal (Palace of Colors).
 
• The Red Fort's design and layout influenced later buildings and gardens in Delhi, Rajasthan, Punjab, Kashmir, and elsewhere.

questions.question: Camels are found in which type of forests in India from the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The thorn forest and scrubs**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Camels** are primarily found in **the thorn forest and scrubs** in India.
 
• Thorn forests and scrubs are characterized by **dry, arid conditions** and are typically found in regions like **Rajasthan**, which is known for its desert landscape.
 
• These forests consist of **thorny trees and bushes** that are well adapted to survive in **harsh, water-scarce environments**.
 
• Camels are well-suited to these conditions due to their ability to **store water and withstand high temperatures**.
 
• In contrast, other types of forests such as **Montane forests, Mangrove forests, and Tropical evergreen forests** do not provide the same suitable habitat for camels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Montane forests** are found in mountainous regions and are characterized by cooler temperatures and higher precipitation.
 
• **Mangrove forests** are coastal wetlands found in tropical and subtropical regions and are known for their salt-tolerant trees and shrubs.
 
• **Tropical evergreen forests** are dense, multi-layered forests that receive high rainfall throughout the year and are found in regions like the Western Ghats and northeastern India.
 
• Each type of forest supports different kinds of flora and fauna, adapted to the specific climatic and geographical conditions of the area.

questions.question: Under whom among the following British Governor -Generals was the new policy of ‘paramountcy’ initiated in British India by the East India Company?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Hastings**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The new policy of **'paramountcy'** was initiated in British India by the East India Company under the British Governor-General **Lord Hastings**.
 
• Lord Hastings served as the Governor-General of India from **1813 to 1823**.
 
• The policy of paramountcy aimed to establish the supremacy of the British East India Company over the Indian states.
 
• It marked a shift from the earlier policy of non-interference to one of active intervention in the affairs of Indian princely states.
 
• This policy laid the foundation for the eventual establishment of British paramountcy over the entire Indian subcontinent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Lord Hastings' real name was **Francis Rawdon-Hastings**, and he was the 1st Marquess of Hastings.
 
• He played a crucial role in the **Third Anglo-Maratha War** (1817-1818), which resulted in the defeat of the Maratha Empire and the expansion of British control in India.
 
• His tenure also saw the implementation of various administrative and military reforms that strengthened British rule in India.
 
• The policy of paramountcy was later continued and expanded by subsequent British Governor-Generals.

questions.question: Paryushana Parva is a festival of which of the following communities?

__
 
• **Paryushana Parva** is a significant festival celebrated by the Jain community.
 
• It is observed for self-purification and upliftment, involving fasting, prayer, and meditation.
 
• The festival typically lasts for 8-10 days, during which Jains engage in various religious activities and rituals.
 
• Paryushana Parva is marked by the practice of forgiveness, where Jains seek forgiveness for any wrongdoings committed during the year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Paryushana** is one of the most important annual festivals for Jains, emphasizing spiritual upliftment and penance.
 
• During this period, Jains focus on the five main vows: non-violence, truth, non-stealing, celibacy, and non-possession.
 
• The festival culminates with the celebration of **Samvatsari**, the Day of Forgiveness, where Jains ask for forgiveness from others.
 
• Different sects of Jainism, such as the Svetambara and Digambara, may celebrate Paryushana at different times and with varying rituals.
 
• The festival fosters a sense of community and encourages Jains to live a life of righteousness and compassion.

questions.question: Who coined the word ‘cell’ in the 1600s, from the Latin word ‘cellula’, meaning ‘small room’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Robert Hooke**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Robert Hooke** coined the term 'cell' in the 1600s.
 
• The term was derived from the Latin word 'cellula', meaning 'small room'.
 
• Hooke made this discovery while observing the structure of cork through a microscope.
 
• He published his findings in his book **Micrographia** in 1665.
 
• Hooke's work laid the foundation for the development of cell theory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Robert Hooke** was an English scientist and a polymath, known for his work in various fields including physics, astronomy, and biology.
 
• His book, **Micrographia**, was one of the first detailed studies using a microscope and included illustrations of his observations.
 
• Hooke's observations of cork cells were the first recorded observations of microscopic life.
 
• He also made significant contributions to the understanding of elasticity, now known as Hooke's Law.
 
• Hooke's work was contemporaneous with other pioneering scientists like Isaac Newton and Antonie van Leeuwenhoek.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of Micro Finance Institutions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Financial service to disadvantaged people**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs)** primarily provide financial services to **disadvantaged people** who lack access to traditional banking services.
 
• These services include **small loans, savings, insurance, and other financial products** aimed at empowering low-income individuals and communities.
 
• MFIs focus on **financial inclusion** by offering credit to people who are typically underserved by conventional financial institutions.
 
• The goal of MFIs is to **alleviate poverty** and promote entrepreneurship among **economically marginalized groups**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Microfinance** originated as a tool to support **small-scale businesses** and **self-employment** ventures in developing countries.
 
• The concept has evolved to include a wide range of financial services that help improve the **economic stability** of low-income populations.
 
• Many MFIs operate on a **non-profit basis**, although there are also for-profit MFIs.
 
• MFIs often employ innovative methods like **group lending** and **peer support** to reduce the risk of default and ensure high repayment rates.

questions.question: The mohororvicic (Moho) discontinuity separates?

options.text: Earth's crust and the inner core

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Earth's crust and the mantle**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Mohorovičić (Moho) discontinuity is the boundary that separates the Earth's crust and the mantle.
 
• It was discovered by Andrija Mohorovičić, a Croatian seismologist, in 1909.
 
• The Moho discontinuity marks a distinct change in seismic wave velocities, indicating a change in composition between the crust and the mantle.
 
• It is located at varying depths beneath the Earth's surface, typically around 35 kilometers beneath continents and about 7-8 kilometers beneath ocean floors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Earth's crust is the outermost solid shell of the planet, composed of a great variety of igneous, metamorphic, and sedimentary rocks.
 
• The mantle lies beneath the crust and extends to a depth of about 2,900 kilometers. It is composed mainly of silicate minerals rich in magnesium and iron.
 
• Seismic waves travel faster through the mantle than through the crust due to the differences in their compositions and densities.
 
• The study of seismic waves and discontinuities like the Moho helps geologists understand the internal structure and composition of the Earth.
